## Why it works

It works as a complete, calm fan install, with the "mistake" as the title's hook. The comments thank it for the job: "I installed my first ceiling fan today all because of this video. Thank you for providing clear and detailed instructions that are beginner friendly." (35 likes) and one viewer learned something about their own house: "now I know why one switch turn on my light only." (9 likes). But the two most-liked comments both name a bigger mistake the video never mentions: "If your replacing a light with a ceiling fan you should make sure that your ceiling electrical box can handle the added weight / vibration and that the box is securely mounted to the ceiling joists. You would not want the fan falling down from the ceiling." (402 likes) and "Before you do anything, after you remove the light fixture, make sure that the box is properly rated and secured to hold the weight of the fan." (149 likes). Others push back on the mistake itself: "There are times that getting all the connections into the box is almost impossible. One example is a fan that has a remote receiver." (59 likes) and "There is an exception in the code that does allow the wires to utilize the canopy space in a box fill calculation." (20 likes). A practical tip that improves the order: make the connections while the fan hangs on the hook, then push them into the box before fixing the motor (45 likes). The pace is fast (about 215 words a minute) but the video is long, and the title promise waits until 9:30. For our use: the confession-style mistake ("it looks natural, that's why you did it") is the shape that transfers; the late payoff and the missing fan-rated-box warning are what to fix.

## Doesn't transfer

- **Other channels' videos as the villain** (ours never knocks other creators or the trade): [0:00] "so there are quite a few ceiling fan installation videos already out there"
- **Announcement:** [0:12] "so in this video I'm going to cover all of that"
- **Pointing at the footage:**
  - [0:24] "it was one of these right here"
  - [1:40] "if you see this Notch out here"
  - [10:45] "as you can see we've got a hole up here"
  - [12:31] "if you look up here at the top of the fan blade mounts"
- **On-camera demonstrations and tests shown:**
  - [4:58] "so I'm going to take a non-contact voltage detector and check each wire"
  - [14:52] "as you can see the fan is now spinning"
- **First-person preference and on-set story:** [4:27] "in my case I prefer for the switch on my left to operate the lights" and [13:17] "I was paying Too Close of attention to the camera"
- **Unsafe (re-energising open wires to identify them; ours uses a method with the power off, or sends it to an electrician):** [4:54] "go ahead turn the circuit breaker back on and then flip on the left switch"
- **Video-link CTA:** [15:27] "I'll post a link to that video right over here"
- **Check against the brief:**
  - The fan-rated, securely fixed box is never mentioned (the two most-liked comments, 402 and 149 likes); our script would treat it as the first check.
  - The splice rule is said as absolute; a commenter (20 likes) says some listed fan canopies count in box fill: [10:07] "all splice points must be contained in a approved electrical box"
  - The stake is vague; the brief should give the real mechanism (a loose or pinched splice in a moving, vibrating canopy): [9:49] "it could create a dangerous situation in the future"
